doc.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Five Spot and Leonard Bernstein
summary: Playing opposite Ornette Coleman, rehearsing with Sonny, and Bernstein's visit.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Were there other places that you could tell us a little bit about? I’m thinking about the Five Spot… think places that are long gone now that people might not know about.
Yeah. Well, part of my thing about wanting to live in the moment is probably because I don’t remember these things. (laughs)
I forget where the… Oh, the Five Spot was over East, right? Yeah.

Yeah, I actually played there with Jim Giuffre, and we played opposite Ornette Coleman’s group there and it was great. And then when I first started working with Sonny Rollins, we rehearsed there in that club. And the Canterino Brothers. (stammers) They, they also had the club just further east of there where it had just opened, and I played there with Sonny Rollins. I can’t remember the name of that club now. But yeah, the Five Spot was great. That was… the… Leonard Bernstein, he would say, (laughs)
said, “You don’t, you don’t buy a Steinway piano. It’s Pete Bernstein and Leonard Bernstein. Remember him saying that?

He had these television shows that he would insist that people call him Bernstein. He says, “You know, E-I in German is ein.” He says, “You don’t buy a Steinway piano.” Anyway, he came in one night and he flipped over Ornette’s group. It was nice.
